findings: The lens-as-learned-model/sensor-as-actuator and illumination/motor-controller alternatives are category errors rather than plausible variants of the biological analogy. Retain the eye/brain distinction but make alternatives comparable.

The wrong options assert names at every edge pixel, complete 3D identities at acquisition, or that no algorithm can ever recognize a chair. These implausible absolutes reveal the carefully qualified key without testing the diagram interpretation.

Every distractor maps line labeling/pictorial structures to unrelated HDR, wavelength/charge conversion, JPEG or pixel-pitch operations. Use competing historical vision representations or purposes, not unrelated camera stages.

Two distractors mix pyramids or regularization with photon-to-charge conversion or guaranteed exact single-image recovery. These are not credible alternatives to multiresolution and smoothness; retain parallel technique-to-purpose mappings.
The physical color-filter array and replacement-for-ADC options are category errors for a probabilistic modeling method. Compare plausible modeling/optimization roles.

Distractors assign deep learning to lens grinding, mechanical shutters or pixel addressing and computational photography to charge transfer. These implausible combinations make the later-period association trivial by elimination.

Two alternatives define a wavelength spectrum as object depth or pixel coordinates and assign unrelated geometric changes. Replace them with plausible spectral-intensity, wavelength and absorption confusions.

The alternatives jump from zero reflectance at one wavelength to creating another wavelength, zero illumination everywhere, or receptor insensitivity to every color. Use plausible confusion among illumination, reflectance and received intensity at the specified wavelength.
Rods-as-lens/cones-as-shutter and depth-versus-mass sensing are implausible biological category errors. Compare sensitivity, color channels and lighting regimes instead.

The carefully qualified radiometric answer is contrasted with unrelated geometry dismissal and reflectance-in-metres claims. The item should discriminate plausible missing wavelength/angular/unit conventions rather than the sole cautious prose.

Shutters storing semantic labels, a lens grid replacing all electronics and software pixels existing before sensing are implausible alternatives to silicon photosites. Use credible distinctions among physical photosites, sampling and reconstructed pixels.

The photosite/retina analogy is in the text bullets below the p934 pipeline, not in the cited figure. Change kind/locator to the actual statement, using the pipeline separately only for its supported signal-conversion relationship.

Every wrong readout option contains unrelated or implausible claims, including red-only versus green-only sensing and an optical lens converting each charge value. Compare credible common-output versus local-conversion/readout architectures.
Unique 3D recovery without processing, JPEG encoding inside the photodiode and route planning without algorithms are not credible alternatives to the shared sensing function.

The key is the only measured source-handling response; distractors infer no silicon/no semiconductor or discard the entire comparison. Test the technical acronym/readout distinction with parallel factual alternatives, not obviously unreasonable editorial choices.
Changing the Bayer pattern or moving the principal point are unrelated to analog gain. Keep plausible gain/exposure/photon-count/noise confusions rather than these category errors.

The world-to-camera-rotation alternative is unrelated to the function of a color filter array. Replace it with a plausible spectral-sampling or reconstruction misconception while retaining the valid missing-channel distinction.
Focus/principal-point errors and camera/object motion are not credible origins for the named sensor charge-noise mechanisms. Compare plausible photon, thermal and readout mechanisms.
Changing the pose matrix and relabeling the principal point cannot plausibly target low-light random graininess. Use competing image-processing choices rather than unrelated geometric labels.
True-depth recovery and retroactive photon collection are category errors for sharpening. The limitation should be tested against plausible edge enhancement, deblurring and noise trade-offs.

White balance determining 3D pose and color correction converting depth to an image row are unrelated geometric operations. Compare channel gains, channel mixing and target color responses with parallel alternatives.

All distractor pairs contain unrelated claims such as compression changing focal length, gamma estimating pose or compression measuring thermal electrons. Compare plausible encoding, quantization and data-reduction roles.

Surface normal equated to principal point and every reflected ray reaching the sensor are weak category/absolute errors. Keep alternatives focused on the physical rear sensor versus the front virtual construction and ray geometry.
Focal length in pixels, depth for every sensor pixel and increasing image row direction are implausible meanings of the drawn surface normal. Use local surface/ray/angular-direction confusions.
ADC brightness sign, Bayer color exchange and physical object rotation are implausible causes of the drawn pinhole inversion. Compare candidate ray paths or rear/front plane conventions.

Demosaicing elimination and automatic world maps are unrelated to the pinhole/lens light-collection trade-off; perfect focus at all depths is an obvious absolute. Use credible aperture, brightness and focus trade-offs.
Changing focus using white-balance gains is a category error. Replace that alternative with a plausible aperture/focus/resolution misconception.

Negative light intensity, every virtual image at the principal point and compulsory pixel focal length do not credibly challenge the signed-distance issue. Compare consistent and inconsistent physical sign conventions.

A camera with a biological crystalline element and an eye with no refracting structure are implausible alternatives. Compare realistic simplified lens arrangements while preserving the stated nonexhaustive-anatomy scope.

The claim that subpixel values are meaningful only at zero depth is not a plausible rounding/indexing rule and contradicts projection domain outright. Keep distractors about continuous coordinates, indexing and interpolation.

List disposal after a call, illegal semicolons and inability to represent a decimal literal are implausible causes of the missing-SE3 error. Use credible import, namespace or execution-order alternatives.
Automatic conversion of P to pixel coordinates and rho changing camera translation are category errors. Compare plausible consequences of rebinding/calibration and execution order.
The alternatives assign geometric constructor arguments to shutter time, cone responses, RGB gain and object size. Use plausible unit/parameter swaps within the camera calibration model.
A principal point storing nearest depth and no front-facing point passing bounds are implausible visibility claims. Compare bounds-only eligibility, depth tests and occlusion explicitly.
The ADC assigning a different focal length to every pixel is unrelated to oblique perspective scaling. Replace it with a credible projection/depth/coordinate misconception.
Nonlinear color correction is unrelated to finite projective vanishing points. Compare parallel direction components, image-plane orientation and degeneracy instead.

NumPy imports retroactively defining every earlier name and plot_point automatically creating the missing camera are implausible execution models. Use realistic import-order and notebook-state alternatives.
Averaging poses or making a grid the camera frame is not plausible under the explicitly supplied per-call override rule. Compare realistic persistent/per-call state behavior.
Estimating mass from brightness and converting geometry into measured RGB are category errors for mkcube/plot_wireframe. Compare credible geometry-generation and projection roles.

Creating all outgoing energy from nothing is an implausible distractor for spectral dispersion. Replace it with a physically meaningful misconception about wavelength mixtures, absorption or refraction.

The p933 citation is kind=figure with locator claiming response integrals and the tristimulus-vector definition. The vector definition is text, while the integrals are on p932; the p933 figure shows weighted response areas. Use separate precise text/equation/figure locators for the premises actually used.

The identical spectral-area/tristimulus locator is attached to p931, which actually shows illuminant E, reflectance R and eye response M, not a spectral-area plot or tristimulus vector. The p932 integrals and p933 text/area plot need page-specific locators and kinds; retain p931 only as the illumination/reflectance premise.

The extra p947 citation points to the right-hand pixel-calibration constructor, which does not state the negative x translation. The relevant p947 evidence is the lower-left move call; alternatively remove the unnecessary p947 citation and retain the p943 inverse-pose premise.

The step says “only the first two” candidates give (2,1). This is already false for the stored display order (o3,o4,o1,o2), and remains unsafe under shuffling. Identify the two vectors or stable option IDs instead. The keyed set o1,o2 is correct.

Absolute horizontal grid coordinates require the grid center. The standalone stem supplies side length, frontal depth and calibration but not X-center=0 or an explicit reference to the source centered grid. For example, center X=0.1 m satisfies the stated dimensions/depth and gives 640,790,940 instead of 490,640,790. Add the missing camera-frame center; the intended key is correct only conditionally.
